Rashi on Ketubot 53b:10:1.hebrew: אלמנה בבית אביה - כלומר מן האירוסין, דאי מן הנשואין לא אמרינן יש לה מזונות, דעד דתלקחן תנן. ואפילו ללוי בנשואין מודה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:10:1.english: A widow in her father’s house - That is to say, [widowed] from betrothal, for if [she was widowed] from marriage, we do not say [that] she has sustenance [from her father’s estate], since we learned [in the Mishnah]: "until they are taken [in marriage]," and even according to Levi, he concedes in [the case of] marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:11:1.hebrew: ת"ק סבר ממאנת אית לה - וה"ק: אלמנה בבית אביה כו', וה"ה לממאנת, דאין כאן נשואין דהא עקרתינהו. ואתא רבי יהודה למימר: עודה בבית אביה בתחלתה, שלא יצתה משם בנשואין, יש לה מזונות, אבל משיצאה בנישואין אין לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:11:1.english: The first tanna maintains [that] a girl who refused [her husband] has [sustenance] - And this is what he is saying: "A widow in her father's house, etc.," and the same applies to a girl who refused [her husband], for there is no marriage here, since she uprooted it. And Rabbi Yehuda comes to say: [when] she is still in her father's house — [meaning] in her initial state, having not left there in marriage — she has sustenance, but once she has left in marriage, she does not have [sustenance].

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:12:1.hebrew: בת יבמה - הכונס את יבמתו וילדה לו בת, יש לה מזונות לאחר מיתת האב מן האחין מנכסי אביה או לא:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:12:1.english: The daughter of a yevama - One who marries his yevama and she bore him a daughter: does she have sustenance after the father's death from the brothers, from her father's property, or not?

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:13:1.hebrew: כיון דאמר מר - כתובתה אינה על נכסי יבם, תנאי כתובה דלה נמי לאו על נכסיו הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:13:1.english: Since the Master said - [that] her marriage contract is not upon the property of the yavam, her marriage contract stipulation is also not upon his property.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:13:2.hebrew: או דלמא - כיון דאמרינן התם, אי לית ליה נכסים לראשון, תקינו לה רבנן משני, כדי שלא תהא קלה בעיניו להוציאה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:13:2.english: Or perhaps - Since we say there [that] if the first [husband] has no property, the Sages enacted for her [to collect] from the second, so that she should not be easy in his eyes to divorce her.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:13:3.english: She has - also the stipulation of the marriage contract, for his daughter to be sustained.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:14:1.hebrew: בת שניה - מי שנשא שניה מדברי סופרים — דאמרי רבנן לקמן בפרק אלמנה (כתובות דף ק:) השניה אין לה כתובה ולא מזונות — בתה שילדה לו ומת:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:14:1.english: A daughter of a secondary [forbidden relative] - [This refers to] one who married a secondary [forbidden relative] by rabbinic decree — [regarding whom] the Sages said later in the chapter [entitled] Almanah (Ketubot 100b): A secondary [forbidden relative] has neither a ketubah nor sustenance — [and this is] her daughter whom she bore to him, and he died.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:14:2.english: [Does] she have sustenance - from his estate or not?

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:1:1.hebrew: שקילא טיבותיך - חיזוק טובותיך שאתה סבור שנחזיק לך טובה בזו, נטולה היא ממך ומוטלת על החרולים:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:1:1.english: Your good is taken - The acknowledgment of your favors — that you think we will be grateful to you for this — is taken from you and cast upon the thorns.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:2:1.hebrew: לרב אע"ג דבגר - בתמיה, והלא בגרות מוציאה מרשות אב, ולמה תיזון מביתו? ובין לרבי בין לר' אלעזר בר' שמעון שנחלקו בדבר בפרק מציאת האשה (לקמן כתובות סח:) בעישור נכסים, מודים במזונות דבין נשאו בין בגרו אבדו מזונות:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:2:1.english: According to Rav, even though [they] became grown women - [This is asked] in astonishment: does not becoming a grown woman remove [a daughter] from [her] father's authority? Why, then, should she be sustained from his house? And according to both Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and Rabbi Elazar beRabbi Shimon — who disagreed about this matter in the chapter [entitled] Metzi'at HaIsha (below, Ketubot 68b) regarding the tenth of the property — they agree regarding sustenance that whether [the daughters] married or became grown women, they have lost [their right to] sustenance.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:3:1.hebrew: כי פליגי בארוסה - רב אמר עד דתלקחן קיחה דאירוסין, ואפילו לא בגר. וללוי, או תבגרן או ינשאו ויצאו מרשות אב לגמרי כי בגרות:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:3:1.english: When they disagree [it is] with regard to a betrothed [daughter] - Rav says [that] "until they are taken" [means] the taking of betrothal, even if they have not become grown women; and according to Levi, either they become grown women or they are married and leave [their] father's authority completely, just as [upon reaching] adulthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:3:2.hebrew: וכן תני לוי במתניתיה - דלוי סידר ברייתא ששה סדרים כר' חייא וכרבי אושעיא:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:3:2.english: And Levi likewise taught in his baraita - For Levi arranged a baraita [of] six orders, like R. Chiya and like Rabbi Oshaya.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:3:4.hebrew: ומטי זמניהון - הגיע זמן שנים עשר חודש לבתולה משתבעה הבעל, כדלקמן באע"פ (כתובות דף נז.):
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:3:4.english: And their time arrives - [This means] the twelve-month period for a virgin from when the husband claims her [for marriage] has arrived, as [stated] below in [the chapter] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 57a).

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:5:1.english: A betrothed woman has sustenance - [Does] a betrothed orphan have sustenance from the brothers, or not?

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:5:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: מסברא לית לה, כיון דאירסה לא ניחא ליה דתיתזיל - מסברא אני אומר שאין לה מזונות מן האחין, דמאי טעמא תקון רבנן מזונות לבת מנכסי האב? כי היכי דלא תיתזיל על הפתחים. הכא ליכא למיחש להכי, דכי חזי ארוס דמתזלא, זיין לה איהו מדידיה, ואע"פ שאינו מחויב לזונה, דכיון דאירסה לא ניחא ליה דתיתזיל:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:5:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: By logical [reasoning] she does not have [sustenance]; since he has betrothed her, it is not satisfactory for him that she be demeaned - By logical [reasoning] I say that she does not have sustenance from the brothers, for what is the reason the Sages instituted sustenance for a daughter from the father's estate? So that she should not be demeaned [by begging] at the doors. Here there is no [need] to be concerned about this, for when the betrother sees that she is being demeaned, he himself will sustain her from his own [means], even though he is not obligated to sustain her, because since he has betrothed her, it is not satisfactory for him that she be demeaned.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:6:1.english: He said to him: If you have not heard [it] - explicitly.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:6:2.hebrew: מסברא אית לה - יש לך לומר שנזונת מן האחים, דארוס לא זיין לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:6:2.english: By logical reasoning she has [sustenance] - You should say that she is sustained by the brothers, for a betrothed [husband] does not feed her.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:6:3.hebrew: כיון דלא קים ליה בגוה - אם תינשא לו, שמא ימצא בה מום, לא שדי זוזי בכדי:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:6:3.english: Since he is not certain about her - If she marries him, perhaps he will find a blemish in her, [so] he will not throw away money for nothing.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:9:1.english: One who refuses - A minor orphan girl whose brothers married her off, and she refused her husband and returned to them.

Rashi on Ketubot 53b:9:2.hebrew: יש לה מזונות - עד שתבגר, או לא? מי אמרינן עקרתינהו לנישואי מעיקרן והויא לה כמי שלא ניסת, או דלמא הא ניסת ויצאה מרשות אב:
Rashi on Ketubot 53b:9:2.english: [Does] she have sustenance - until she reaches majority, or not? Do we say [that] she uprooted the marriage from its inception, and she is like one who was never married, or perhaps she has already married and left [her] father's authority?

Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:10:1.hebrew: אלמנה בבית אביה - פירש בקונטרס דהיינו מן האירוסין, דמן הנשואין לכולי עלמא לית לה, דכיון שנפקעה שעה אחת ממזונות, שוב אין לה, אבל מן האירוסין לא פקעי, דקסבר ארוסה יש לה מזונות. וא"ת: א"כ, אמאי נקט "אלמנה", כיון דאפילו לא נתאלמנה יש לה מזונות? ויש לומר: לאשמועינן אבל מן הנשואין אפילו נתאלמנה אין לה; אי נמי, לאשמועינן דוקא אלמנה מן האירוסין יש לה, מן הנשואין אין לה, אבל ממאנת — אע"ג דנשאת אית לה, ואתי שפיר הא דאמר: "ממאנת איכא בינייהו". ואם תאמר: ובשומרת יבם מאי אתא לאשמועינן? דאי למידק דוקא מן האירוסין, אבל מן הנישואין לא — מאי איריא שומרת יבם? אפילו אלמנה שאינה זקוקה ליבם נמי אין לה! ויש לומר דנקט שומרת יבם לרבותא: דלא מיבעיא ארוסה, דאכתי מיחסרא מסירה לחופה, אלא אפי' שומרת יבם, דלא מיחסרא, שיכול לבא עליה בעל כרחה — אפי' הכי יש לה מזונות. ורבינו תם מפרש: "אלמנה בבית אביה" — שהיתה נשואה, ונתאלמנה או נתגרשה בחיי אביה; והיינו "בבית אביה" יש לה מזונות, הואיל כשנתאלמנה או נתגרשה אכתי לא מת האב ולא בא זמן חיוב מזונות, ולא מיפסיד מידי. ודייק דממאנת לת"ק מ"בית אביה" נפקא: דמדאתא רבי יהודה לטפויי, למימר ד"עודה בבית אביה" בעינן, מכלל דת"ק ד"בית אביה" אפילו יצתה, והיינו בכה"ג דמיאנה, דעקרתינהו לנשואין קמאי והרי היא כאילו לא נשאת מעולם. ואין נראה, דכיון דנשאת, שוב אין לה מזונות, דאין לאב רשות בה; ופירוש הקונטרס נראה עיקר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:10:1.english: "A widow in her father's house" - Rashi explained that this refers to [a widow] from betrothal [erusin], for [one widowed] from full marriage [nisuin] does not have [sustenance] according to everyone — since once she has been removed from [her father's] sustenance for even one hour, she no longer has [it]; however, from betrothal [her right] does not cease, for he holds [that] a betrothed woman has [a right to] sustenance. And if you ask: If so, why did [the baraita] specify "a widow," since even if she was not widowed she has sustenance? One can answer: [It comes] to teach us [that] from full marriage, however, even if she was widowed, she does not have [sustenance]. Alternatively, [it comes] to teach us [that] specifically a widow from betrothal has [sustenance, whereas one] from full marriage does not have [it], whereas a woman who refuses [her husband — mema'enet] — even though she was married, she has [sustenance]; and this fits well with that which [the Gemara] says [below]: "A woman who refuses is [the difference] between them." And if you ask: And regarding a widow awaiting her yavam, what does [the baraita] come to teach us? For if [it were] to infer [that] specifically [one] from betrothal [has sustenance], whereas [one] from full marriage does not — why specifically a widow awaiting her yavam? Even a widow who is not bound to a yavam also does not have [sustenance]! One can answer that [the baraita] mentioned a widow awaiting her yavam as a novelty: that it is unnecessary [to state] a betrothed woman, who still lacks delivery to the marriage canopy [chuppah], rather even a widow awaiting her yavam, who does not lack [this], since [the yavam] can have relations with her against her will — even so, she has sustenance. And Rabbeinu Tam explains: "A widow in her father's house" — [means] that she was married [nisuin], and was widowed or divorced during her father's lifetime; and this is [the meaning of] "in her father's house, she has sustenance" — since when she was widowed or divorced, the father had not yet died and the time of the obligation of sustenance had not yet arrived, and nothing was lost. And he infers that a woman who refuses [mema'enet] is derived according to the first Tanna from "in her father's house": for since Rabbi Yehuda comes to add, to say that we require "she is still in her father's house," it follows by implication that [according to] the first Tanna, "in her father's house" [applies] even if she left [it] — and this is in a case such as where she refused [her husband], for she uprooted the first marriage retroactively, and behold she is as though she had never been married. However, [this] does not appear [correct], for once she has been married, she no longer has sustenance, since the father [no longer] has authority over her; and Rashi's explanation appears primary.

Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:12:1.hebrew: בת יבמה יש לה מזונות או אין לה מזונות - נראה דיבמה עצמה פשיטא ליה דיש לה מזונות, דגבי דידה אמרינן תנאי כתובה ככתובה, וכי לית ליה לראשון, תקינו לה גם מזונות משני. אבל בת — מיבעיא ליה אי אלימא כמותה למהוי תנאי כתובה ככתובה, וכגון דלית ליה לראשון, דאי אית ליה — ממה נפשך גביא. ובכה"ג אזלה בעיא דבת שניה, דפשיטא ליה דשניה עצמה לית לה, דלגבי דידה הוי תנאי כתובה ככתובה, אבל גבי בת מיבעיא לן. וי"מ, דאף בדאית ליה לראשון קבעי: אע"ג דלדידה פשיטא דאית לה מזונות בין אית ליה בין לית ליה כדפי', בבתו מיבעיא ליה. דמראשון ודאי לית לה, שהרי הוא לא כתב לה אלא "בנן נוקבן דיהויין ליכי מינאי אינון יתבין", והאי לאו מיניה היא; אבל מן השני — דלמא אית לה, כיון דאי לית לה מראשון תקינו לה משני דכל תנאי יהיו על השני מוטלין, ולענין מזונות הבת — אע"ג דאית ליה לראשון, כיון שאינה נזונת מהם כמאן דלית ליה דמי, ותקינו לה רבנן משני; או דלמא משני נמי לית לה. וצריך עיון אי הוה מצי למיבעי נמי לענין כתובת בנין דכרין: דדלמא לית לה, דהא מאחיו ירית, או דלמא איכא למיחש דלמא מימנע האב ולא יהיב, דחייש דלמא נפלה לה קמיה יבם. ומיהו אארוסה נראה דלא הוה מצי למיבעי לענין כתובת בנין דכרין, דהא לא יהיב לה אב מידי כל זמן שהיא ארוסה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:12:1.english: The daughter of a yevama: Does she have sustenance, or does she not have sustenance? - It appears that regarding the yevama herself, it is obvious to him [that] she has sustenance, for regarding her we say [that] the stipulations of a ketubah are like the ketubah [itself], and when the first [husband] has nothing, [the Sages] enacted for her sustenance from the second [husband, i.e., the yavam] as well. However, [regarding her] daughter, he asks whether [her right] is as strong as hers [such] that [her sustenance] is [treated under the rule that] the stipulations of a ketubah are like the ketubah [itself] — and [this dilemma applies] in a case where the first [husband] has no [property], for if he has [property], she collects either way. And in this same manner goes the dilemma regarding the daughter of a secondary forbidden relationship [sheniyah]: for it is obvious to him that the sheniyah herself has no [sustenance], since regarding her, the stipulations of a ketubah are like the ketubah [itself]; however, regarding [her] daughter, we have a dilemma. And there are those who explain that he asks even where the first [husband] has [property]: even though regarding [the mother] herself it is obvious that she has sustenance whether [the first husband] has [property] or does not have [property], as explained [earlier], he asks regarding his daughter. For from the first [husband] she certainly has nothing, since he only wrote to her, "Female children that you will have from me, they shall dwell [in my house]," and this [daughter] is not from him; but from the second [husband], perhaps she does have [sustenance], since when [the yevama] has nothing from the first [husband], [the Sages] enacted for her from the second [husband] that all stipulations [of the ketubah] are incumbent upon the second [husband] — and regarding the daughter's sustenance, even though the first [husband] has [property], since she cannot be sustained from [his property], it is considered as though he has nothing, and the Rabbis enacted [sustenance] for her from the second [husband] — or perhaps from the second [husband] as well she has nothing. And it requires further study whether he could also have asked regarding the ketubah of male children [ketubat benin dikhrin]: [for] perhaps she does not have [that stipulation], since [the yavam] inherits from his brother; or perhaps there is reason to be concerned lest the father refrain and not give [a dowry], because he fears that [his daughter] might fall before a yavam. However, regarding a betrothed woman [arusah], it appears that he could not have asked regarding the ketubah of male children, since the father does not give her anything as long as she is betrothed.

Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:4:1.hebrew: הויה דאירוסין או הויה דנשואין - הכא ליכא למיפרך: "אי הויה דנשואין היא, אע"ג דבגר?", כדפריך לעיל לרב דתני "עד דתלקחן"; דהתם פריך משום דמשמע דאתא לאפוקי מדלוי. אבל הכא, רב יוסף תני ברייתא באפי נפשה, וקמשמע לן נישאת כשהיא קטנה, והוא הדין לאיבגר ולא אינסיב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:4:1.english: Becoming betrothed or becoming married - Here one cannot object: "If it is becoming married, [is she sustained] even though she became a grown woman?" — as [the Gemara] objected above against Rav, who taught "until they are taken [in marriage]"; for there it objected because it implies that [Rav] comes to exclude [the view] of Levi. But here, Rav Yosef teaches a baraita on its own, and it teaches us [the law of one who] married while she was a minor, and the same applies to [one who] became a grown woman and was not married.

Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:5:1.hebrew: ארוסה יש לה מזונות או אין לה מזונות - לא שמיע ליה פלוגתא דתנאי דלעיל, אי נמי שמיע ליה ומבעיא ליה היכי הלכתא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 53b:5:1.english: "Does a betrothed [orphan] have sustenance, or does she not have sustenance?" - He had not heard the dispute of the Tannaim [cited] above; or alternatively, he had heard it, and he was asking what the halakha is.
